title: Campaigns OS QA Verdict v0
description: The full QA verdict `campaigns-os qa run` writes under qa-output/<map-id>/<run-id>.json and publishes to the QA portal receiver. Contract identity is campaigns-os-qa-verdict/v0; the emitted schema_version FIELD is the literal "1.0" (it predates the slash-versioned naming convention, and the receiving Worker validates that same literal — changing the emitted value is a breaking shape change). Additions to v0 are expected; consumers must tolerate unknown fields, so additionalProperties stays true. Full verdicts carry live storefront URLs, request evidence, and order references and are gitignored — the committed form is the allowlist projection described by campaigns-os-qa-verdict-sidecar.v0.schema.json. Trust semantics: the CLI never emits trusted/trust_level/verified_at; the QA verdict receiver stamps them server-side at ingest, so they appear only on records read back from the portal. Schema-validity is NOT trust — a forged record can be shape-valid. Every downstream consumer MUST filter or segregate records carrying trusted: false. See docs/qa-and-test-orders.md (Verdict schema and trust semantics).

schema_version.description: The emitted schema-version literal. "1.0" is the campaigns-os-qa-verdict/v0 shape; both src/qa-verdict.mjs validateVerdict and the portal receiver reject any other value.

run_id.description: The QA run identity, also the verdict filename under qa-output/<map-id>/. The portal receiver additionally restricts it to [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}.

campaign_slug.description: Carries the Campaign Map ID for schema back-compat; the true public route slug rides alongside as public_route_slug so consumers stop conflating the two.

public_route_slug.description: The campaign's public route slug. null (or absent on verdicts emitted before the field existed) when no slug was resolved.

campaign_ref_id.description: The platform campaign ref id from the CampaignSpec, when available.

spec_version.description: CampaignSpec schema version the run validated against (e.g. "4.3"), or a runner-scoped marker such as "parity-fixture-<version>" for fixture-driven parity runs.

spec_hash.description: Hash of the CampaignSpec the run used, prefixed with the algorithm (e.g. "sha256:<hex>").

started_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp the QA run started.

completed_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp the verdict was finalized.

operator.description: Best-effort local operator identity (e.g. "<user>@local"). Empty string when unresolvable. NOT verified attribution — see the trust fields.

base_url.description: The --base-url or packet deploy URL the run resolved pages against. Omitted when the run had none. URL-bearing: emptied from the committed sidecar projection.

entry_urls.description: One entry-page reference per funnel topology. URL-bearing: emptied ([]) in the committed sidecar projection.

page_urls.description: Every resolved page URL across the run's funnel topologies, deduplicated by URL. URL-bearing: emptied ([]) in the committed sidecar projection.

tested_urls.description: Pages that produced an http:<page_id> assertion, joined back to the known page references. URL-bearing: emptied ([]) in the committed sidecar projection.

disposition.description: Derived from the assertions (and the commercial section's status): any unwaived failing blocker => blocked; any warn/manual_review/waived assertion or a proven commercial mismatch => ready_with_exceptions; otherwise ready. Waived is never clean. ready_with_waivers is the doctor/next checkpoint term, never a verdict disposition.

assertions.description: The flat assertion list every QA leg serializes into. The portal receiver caps validation at 500 entries.

test_orders.description: One entry per typed-card browser test order the run drove, with persisted-order verification and sanitized request evidence.

exceptions.description: Derived projection of every assertion that failed, warned, needs manual review, or carries warn/blocker severity — the quick exception read without re-scanning assertions.

commercial.description: The commercial parity section, present on runs where calculate scenarios were planned (or explicitly recorded as unavailable). Absent on verdicts emitted before the leg existed.

trusted.description: SERVER-STAMPED, never CLI-emitted: the QA verdict receiver classifies each submission at ingest and stamps the stored record. false means the record arrived without the ingest credential (an anonymous submission) — shape-valid but unattributed. Present only on records read back from the receiver. Every downstream consumer MUST filter or segregate records with trusted: false; campaigns-os itself refuses to promote such a record into the committed sidecar and excludes it from run-record verdict inference.

trust_level.description: SERVER-STAMPED companion to trusted: how the submission authenticated. anonymous pairs with trusted: false; shared_secret pairs with trusted: true.

verified_at.description: SERVER-STAMPED companion to trusted: ISO 8601 instant the receiver verified the ingest credential. null on untrusted records.

pageUrlRef.description: A funnel-topology page reference: identity fields plus the resolved live URL.

family.description: The canonical assertion-family vocabulary (QA_ASSERTION_FAMILY_VOCABULARY in src/qa-verdict.mjs; a drift test asserts set equality against the emitters). Append-only: a new emitter family is an additive schema change.

page.description: The page_id or label the assertion is about, or the reserved value "campaign" for campaign-level assertions.

url.description: The live page URL the assertion ran against, when page-scoped. URL-bearing: stripped from the committed sidecar projection.

severity.description: Present on issue-bearing assertions. The portal receiver requires it when status is fail or warn.

evidence.description: Free-form structured evidence for this assertion (gate codes, capture summaries, blocked_by references, step ladders). Shape varies by family and is not individually contracted here. Stripped from the committed sidecar projection.

waiver.description: A bounded named-human waiver riding an assertion. Any assertion carrying one keeps the disposition at ready_with_exceptions — waived is never clean.

url.description: URL-bearing: null/absent in the committed sidecar projection.

exception.description: deriveExceptions output: the source assertion's identity fields. Values are nullable because the projection copies whatever the assertion carried.

path.description: The planned order path, e.g. "checkout", "accept", "accept-decline-accept", or a tier/coupon plan label such as "checkout@tier:8".

plan.description: Summary of a spec-derived tier/coupon plan (--test-order tiers), when the order ran under one.

qa_email.description: Always the redaction marker ("[redacted-qa-email]") — the generated QA email itself never enters the verdict.

card.description: Card last4 only; full test-card numbers never enter the verdict.

verification.description: Persisted-order read-back verification — the authoritative proof path.

steps.description: The step-ladder: ordered, individually timed named steps ({step, status, started_at, duration_ms, detail?, evidence?, error?}), appended as each finishes so a crash still leaves the ladder up to the failure point.

events.description: Sanitized network/console event capture. Checkout request bodies and generated QA emails are redacted before serialization.

status.description: mismatch keeps the verdict at ready_with_exceptions; incomplete preserves the disposition derived from ordinary assertions and never invents an exception.

findings.description: Proven contract-governed claim mismatches, serialized deterministically into the flat assertions array as warn-severity pricing assertions.

issues.description: Sanitized capture/proxy/limit issue codes with counts. An issue records incomplete evidence; it never invents a mismatch.

commercial.description: The compact commercial-parity report: counters over checked pages, scenarios, and claims, plus findings and issues. Counter fields are additive and not individually contracted here.
